run.question: The payment-api pod in namespace app-259 had issues on November 23, 2026 around 13:45 UTC. What happened?

report.summary: Only the Loki log source was reachable in this Run (Prometheus, Jaeger and the Kubernetes API all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so the assessment rests on payment-api's own container logs. Observed: in namespace app-259 the logs come from a single pod, payment-api-259-d8f7b9c4-abc12 (service payment-api, job payment-api). From 2026-11-22T12:14 through 2026-11-23T13:42 every returned line is INFO "Payment processed successfully"; the first logged error is at 2026-11-23T13:46:00 UTC and reads "Failed to acquire database connection - pool exhausted" (wait_time_ms 1227, queue_length 10). That identical ERROR message repeats 8 times up to 14:44 (wait_time_ms 1227-4840, queue_length 5-15); it is the only ERROR message returned in the 13:00-15:00 window and comes from one stream. Successful payments are interleaved (13:59 PAY-1800; 14:49 PAY-8206; 15:27 PAY-4120), so this was partial degradation, not a total outage of the pod. What happened is therefore a database connection-pool exhaustion inside the payment-api pod starting ~13:46 UTC and logged until 14:44; why the pool was exhausted (database-side slowness/unavailability versus pool sizing or a connection leak) could not be determined, because no database-side logs, no Prometheus metrics, no traces and no Kubernetes objects/events/configmaps were retrievable. A restart, crash, OOM or config change cannot be confirmed or excluded from the available evidence; no startup/shutdown/OOM lines were returned by Loki between 2026-11-20 and 16:20, which is a gap rather than proof.

claims.text: All log lines returned for namespace app-259 come from one pod stream: pod_name payment-api-259-d8f7b9c4-abc12, service payment-api, job payment-api; no other pod_name, service or namespace appeared in the returned log lines or in the per-namespace/per-service line-count series for 13:00-14:00.

The pre-incident baseline is clean: 32 log lines returned between 2026-11-22T12:14:00 and 2026-11-23T13:42:00 UTC are all level INFO "Payment processed successfully" (e.g. PAY-5032 at 13:42), with no ERROR line in that set.

The first observed failure is at 2026-11-23T13:46:00 UTC on pod payment-api-259-d8f7b9c4-abc12: level ERROR, message "Failed to acquire database connection - pool exhausted", wait_time_ms 1227, queue_length 10.

The same ERROR message "Failed to acquire database connection - pool exhausted" repeats 8 times between 13:46:00 and 14:44:00 UTC (13:46, 13:54, 14:03, 14:15, 14:19, 14:21, 14:31, 14:44) with wait_time_ms between 1227 and 4840 and queue_length between 5 and 15; these are all the ERROR lines and the only stream returned for 13:00-15:00.

Successful payments were still logged during and after the error burst by the same pod: INFO "Payment processed successfully" PAY-1800 at 13:59, PAY-8206 at 14:49 and PAY-4120 at 15:27 UTC; the newest sampled log line is 15:27.

The pod was not fully failing: "Payment processed successfully" lines at 13:59 (during the 13:46-14:44 error burst) and at 14:49 show requests still completing, so the pool exhaustion affected only part of the traffic observed.

The failures originate from exhaustion of payment-api's own database connection pool: callers waited up to ~4.8 s and up to 15 requests queued for a connection before the acquire attempt failed. The trigger of the exhaustion (database-side slowness/unavailability versus pool size or a leaked connection) is not established by the available evidence.

A degraded or slow database dependency could be holding connections open longer, producing the exhausted pool on the client side; this remains untested because no database-side logs, metrics or traces were retrievable in this Run.

A pod lifecycle event (restart, OOM kill or config rollout) behind the 13:46 onset is neither supported nor excluded: Loki returned no startup, shutdown, SIGTERM or OOM lines for app-259 between 2026-11-20 and 16:20, and Kubernetes objects and events could not be read.

Check the payment-api Deployment's database connection-pool settings (max pool size, acquire timeout) and any pool-related ConfigMap together with database-side latency/connection metrics, to distinguish pool sizing from a slow database before any remediation is chosen.

Restore or grant access to Prometheus, Jaeger and the Kubernetes API for this environment so pod restart counts, container termination reasons, events and span-level dependency latency for payment-api can be examined during 13:40-14:45 UTC.

gaps: Kubernetes API was unreachable (kubernetes_jq_query, kubernetes_count and fetch_pod_logs all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE at 2026-11-23T16:24Z), so pod status, container lastState/exit codes, restart counts, events, Deployment/ReplicaSet ownership, Service/Endpoint/NetworkPolicy objects and ConfigMaps could not be inspected.

Prometheus was unreachable (get_metric_names, get_metric_target/get_prometheus_target, execute_prometheus_instant_query and metrics_range_query all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so no request-rate, error-rate or latency series exist for payment-api or any database dependency in this Run.
Jaeger was unreachable (traces_search and traces_list_services returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so no trace evidence of which downstream/database call was slow or failing at 13:45 UTC.

Loki returned log streams only for service payment-api in namespace app-259; no other namespace or service (including any database component) returned lines for the incident period, so the database side of the failed connection acquisitions is unobservable.

Absence statements rest on queries that returned no data and are therefore unknown, not zero: a query for level="ERROR" in 14:45-16:20 UTC, a query for "pool exhausted" in 2026-11-01..2026-11-22T23:59, a query for level="WARN" in 12:00-16:20, and a query for start/shutdown/OOM lines in 2026-11-20..2026-11-23T16:20 all returned nothing. Log retention and the sparse, roughly minute-level sampling of this pod's logs limit what can be concluded from them.

The trigger of the connection-pool exhaustion (database-side fault, pool configuration, or connection leak) and the exact end of the episode are unresolved; the newest error line observed is 14:44 and the newest line overall is a success at 15:27 UTC.
